Actor.description: Who sent a command: user, agent:<client name> or cli.

config.description: A custom protocol as JSON: the "pulse-code" or "preset" family (doc 06).

reason.description: Why the channels were put together (or left alone), in plain words.

alternatives.description: Other candidates, for comparison and learning.

chosen.description: The best non-overlapping explanation of the bus, most confident first.

unexplained.description: Channels of the bus that no detection explains.

i2cFirstByte.description: The first byte read as an I2C address byte, when that makes sense.

pairs.description: Pairs read as 16-bit values, when the bytes are not text.

hex.description: Hex as typed by a person: "48 65 6C", "0x48,0x65".

limits.description: Rate limits by number of enabled channels, fewest channels first.

maxSamples.description: Most samples per channel in one capture, where limited (buffer depth).

outputs.description: Outputs (PWM); added with the first device that has them (M3).

threshold.description: Adjustable threshold: lowest, highest and step in volts.

notes.description: Observations across buses (a TX/RX pair), and why the window is short if it is.

oneOf.description: Record to device memory, then download.

title.description: The tab title; "Capture N" when absent.

wait.description:
Wait until the capture ends (default). Without waiting, the capture runs on and
`capture.done` follows.

capture.description: The finished capture, when waited for.

artefact.description: Samples left out of analysis (a start-up artefact).

savedDecoders.description: Decoder settings found in the file: for comparison, never used by detection.

unsaved.description:
Closing it loses something: a capture from a device that was never saved, or decoders,
markers, names or groups changed since the file was opened or saved.

all.description: Replaces every group at once (what an undo uses).

channels.description: Its channels; none or empty removes the group. A channel leaves any other group.

bursts.description: Stretches of activity, split at pauses longer than `burst_gap`.

glitches.description: Pulses well under half the narrowest repeated width.

highFraction.description: Fraction of the active stretch spent high.

narrowest.description: Narrowest pulse that occurs repeatedly (single glitches ignored).

CommandError.description: An error worded for the person or agent: what is wrong and what to do.

decoder.description: A decoder id on the capture.

text.description: Contained in the label or detail (any case).

id.description: The decoder id to use (redo and undo use the id it had); a new one when absent.

protocol.description: A protocol id from protocol.list, such as "i2c".

roles.description: Role to physical channel, such as {"scl": 5, "sda": 4}.

DecoderConfig.description: A decoder's configuration: what `decoder.add` takes and an undo restores.

explain.description: Group the problems and explain likely causes.

packets.description: Packets (a UART line, an I2C transaction) instead of single frames.

problems.description: Only frames (or packets with frames) that have problems.

text.description: Only items whose label, detail, title or text contains this (any case).

total.description: Items that match, over all pages.

replaceSettings.description: Replace all settings instead of merging (what an undo uses).

settings.description: Settings to change; the others keep their values.

channels.description: Physical channels this detection explains, ascending.

notes.description: Why each setting (or role, keyed "role:<key>") has its value.

capturing.description: Whether a capture is running on it.

holder.description: Who holds the lease, if anyone.

id.description: Stable id, such as "synthetic/mix" or a USB serial.

device.description: A device id from device.list, such as "synthetic/mix".

oneOf.description: The input does not match the contract or is impossible ("300 MHz with 20 channels").
A capture, decoder, marker, device or history entry that does not exist.
The device is leased by someone else, or a capture is running.
Outputs are switched off, or an agent's actions are paused by the person.
Asked for something this command cannot do (undo of a file write).
Anything else; the message says what happened and what to do.
Also after undo, redo, open and close.
Read the session again: after any recorded command, undo, redo or lease change.

supports.description: Whether the observation supports the protocol or counts against it.

causes.description: Symptoms, causes and actions for this protocol (doc 06, symptom tables).

id.description: The capture id to use (redo uses the id it had); a new one when absent.

path.description: A path on the machine running the engine.

title.description: The tab title; the file name when absent.

path.description: Where to save; a path ending in .lacap. Without it, the .lacap the capture came from.

detail.description: Longer explanation for the table and tooltips.

label.description: Short label under the waveform, such as "4F".

packet.description: Index of the packet it belongs to.

row.description: Annotation row under the lane: 0 for bytes and fields, 1 for single bits.

HistoryEntry.description: One entry of the engine-wide history (ADR 0008).

discarded.description: Undone, and then the same actor did something new: it can no longer be redone.

inverse.description: `None` when the command cannot be undone.

neverBecause.description: Why it cannot be undone, when it cannot.

summary.description: Plain-language line for the activity feed: "Claude added an I2C decoder on CH4 and CH5".

entry.description: A history entry by id; without it, the actor's own last action.

what.description: What was found: a frame label, "rising edge on CH5", "high pulse of 80 ns on CH3".

Invocation.description: A command call as data: what the history stores and `run_command` takes.

at.description: Sample of the marker, or the start of a range note.

by.description: Who placed it; agents' markers carry an "agent" badge in the window.
Who placed it, when an undo restores someone else's marker (honoured for the person only).

id.description: The marker id to use (redo and undo use the id it had); a new one when absent.

moveView.description: Move the view so the marker is in the middle.

frequencyHz.description: 1 ÷ the time, when it is not zero.

limit.description: Edges per page (default 1,000, at least 64, at most 10,000).

glitches.description: Pulses well under half the narrowest repeated width.

note.description: Set when only part of the range was measured.

Note.description: Format surprises, dropped data, artefacts: shown to the person and in MCP summaries.

Nothing.description: Input of commands that take nothing.

Packet.description: A group of frames (a UART line, an I2C transaction, a chip-select frame) with its bytes.

text.description: Every stream as text, labelled: "Write to 0x57: ·· | Read from 0x57: CALIBRATED 2026".

paused.description: true stops agents' capture and output commands; false lets them run again.

stopped.description: Captures started by agents that were stopped by this switch.

continuous.description: The signal never pauses between its first and last edge and spans most of the window.

periodSamples.description: Average rising-to-rising period inside bursts, in samples.

pulsesPerBurst.description: Clock pulses per burst (bursts split at pauses longer than 3 periods).

regularity.description: Fraction of periods within a few percent of the typical one (1 = perfectly regular).

first.description: Sample of the first one, to jump to.

ProtocolInfo.description: What the person (or agent) can learn about a protocol from the tool itself.

confirm.description: How to confirm it on the waveform.

decoderTips.description: What to set in the decoder.

lookalikes.description: What else looks similar and how to tell them apart.

what.description: What it is and where you meet it.

Query.description:
A search (doc 06): a typed structure, not a text grammar. `decoded`, `edge` and `pulse` produce
hits; `within`, `level`, `not` and further producers filter them inside `all`.

from.description: First sample; after the start-up artefact when absent.

to.description: End sample (exclusive); the end of the detection window when absent.

RateLimit.description: The fastest rate with up to `max_channels` channels enabled.

from.description: First sample; the person's view when absent.

to.description: End sample (exclusive); the person's view, or the whole capture, when absent.

rows.description: What the picture shows, top to bottom: the time axis, channels, decoder rows, markers.

noun.description: Short noun for setup messages: "the data line" in "Choose a channel for the data line."

SavedDecoder.description: Decoder settings found in an imported file: shown for comparison, never used by detection.

channels.description: Role name to physical channel; `None` where the file leaves it unassigned.

options.description: Option name to value, as text.

protocol.description: The file's own protocol name, normalised to lower case (`uart`, `i2c`, `spi`, …).

truncated.description: More hits exist than were returned.

active.description: The capture whose tab is in front.

agentsPaused.description: Agents' capture and output commands are refused (the person's "stop agent actions").

recent.description: The latest history entries, newest first.

revision.description: Grows with every change; `state.changed` events carry it.

SettingValue.description: A setting's value: a number, a choice (text) or a switch.

detail.description: For example "FNIRSI .demo file mystery_D.demo" or "synthetic device, program mix".

Span.description: A half-open stretch of samples; fractional ends come from averaged periods.

View.description: A tab's view (doc 08): the visible range, cursors and selection.

activate.description: Bring this capture's tab to the front.

frames.description: Frames in the range, when there are few enough to draw one by one.

spans.description: Otherwise stretches of frames closer than a bucket, as (start, end, any problem).

counts.description: Otherwise transitions per bucket of `bucket` samples from `from`.

edges.description: Every edge in the range (first samples at a new level), when there are few enough to draw.

levels.description: And the level at the start of each bucket: "0" or "1" per bucket.

channels.description: Physical channels; the visible ones when absent.

to.description: End sample (exclusive); limited to the capture's length.

WidthCluster.description: A group of similar pulse widths.

analysis.bytes.summary: What a run of bytes might mean: text, hidden text, Modbus, checksums, BCD, 16-bit pairs.

analysis.detect.summary: Measure channels, group them into buses and detect protocols with evidence, for the whole capture or a range.

capture.close.summary: Close a capture and free its memory.

undo.reason: Closing drops the capture; open it again from its file.

capture.start.summary: Start a capture with the device's configuration; the capture appears while it streams in.

undo.reason: Captured data cannot be undone; close the capture instead.

channel.group.summary: Put channels into a named bus group, or ungroup them.

decoder.add.summary: Add a decoder (protocol, roles, settings), or one from a detection; undo removes it.

decoder.frames.summary: Decoded packets or frames by time range, kind, problem and text, paged; optionally explained.

decoder.remove.summary: Remove a decoder; undo restores it with the same id.

decoder.update.summary: Change a decoder's roles or settings; returns how its problem counts changed.

device.configure.summary: Set channels, rate, length, mode and threshold; rejected with a reason when impossible.

device.connect.summary: Connect a device and take its lease; returns its capabilities.

device.disconnect.summary: Disconnect a device and release its lease.

device.list.summary: Connected and available devices with capabilities, lease holders and setup hints.

file.open.summary: Open a capture file (.lacap, .demo, .sr, .vcd) from a path on this machine; undo closes it.

file.save.summary: Save a capture as .lacap, or export it as .sr or VCD.

undo.reason: Writing a file cannot be undone.

history.list.summary: Recent history entries with actors, newest first.

history.redo.summary: Redo the actor's own last undone action, or any entry by id.

history.undo.summary: Undo the actor's own last action, or any entry by id.

lease.take.summary: Take a device's lease (the person can always take it from an agent).

marker.add.summary: Add a marker or range note (with an agent badge when an agent adds it); optionally move the view there.

marker.remove.summary: Remove a marker; undo restores it with the same id.

marker.update.summary: Change a marker's label, note or place.

measure.edges.summary: Edges of chosen channels in a range, paged.

measure.stats.summary: Frequency, period, duty, pulse widths and edge count of a channel in a range.

protocol.addCustom.summary: Add a custom JSON protocol (pulse-code or preset) for this session.

undo.reason: Custom protocols are removed with protocol.removeCustom.

protocol.info.summary: What a protocol is, how to confirm it, decoder tips, lookalikes and symptoms.

protocol.list.summary: Every protocol the engine knows, with its roles and settings.

render.summary: A PNG image of a time range with decoder rows and markers, for agents that can see images.

search.run.summary: Search edges and decoded content with a typed query; hits with times.

session.get.summary: Open captures and their state, decoders with problem counts, markers, views, leases, recent activity.

session.pauseAgents.summary: The person's switch to stop agents' capture and output commands, and to let them run again.

undo.reason: A safety switch, not an edit; switch it back instead.

view.set.summary: Move a tab's view: visible range, cursors A and B, selection.

waveform.get.summary: What to draw for a range: per channel the edges, or level-of-detail buckets when zoomed out, and decoder frames.
